question: Three distinct lines \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) lie in the same plane, with \(a\parallel b\) and \(c\) intersecting \(a\). How many intersection points do these three lines have in total?
solution: If \(c\) did not intersect \(b\), then \(c\parallel b\). Together with \(a\parallel b\), this would imply \(c\parallel a\), contradicting the fact that \(c\) and \(a\) intersect. Therefore, \(c\) also intersects \(b\). Lines \(a\) and \(b\) do not intersect, so there are 2 intersection points in total.
